events.title: Crusaders defeat the Seljuk Turks at Dorylaeum
events.description: The First Crusade routed the army of Kilij Arslan I at Dorylaeum in Anatolia. The victory opened the road across Asia Minor and showed that the crusaders could beat the Seljuks in open battle.
events.html: The First Crusade routed the army of Kilij Arslan I at Dorylaeum in Anatolia. The victory opened the road across Asia Minor and showed that the crusaders could beat the Seljuks in open battle.

events.title: Castile wins a modest victory at La Higueruela near Granada
events.description: The army of John II of Castile, led by Álvaro de Luna, defeated the forces of the Nasrid emir Muhammad IX outside Granada but did not take the city. Castile instead installed a rival claimant, Yusuf IV, as emir.
events.html: The army of John II of Castile, led by Álvaro de Luna, defeated the forces of the Nasrid emir Muhammad IX outside Granada but did not take the city. Castile instead installed a rival claimant, Yusuf IV, as emir.

events.title: William III defeats James II at the Battle of the Boyne
events.description: William of Orange defeated the deposed James II on the River Boyne in Ireland (1 July Old Style). The victory secured the Protestant succession and is still commemorated by the Orange Order each July.
events.html: William of Orange defeated the deposed James II on the River Boyne in Ireland (1 July Old Style). The victory secured the Protestant succession and is still commemorated by the Orange Order each July.

events.title: Lexell's Comet passes closer to Earth than any comet on record
events.description: The comet Charles Messier had discovered in June passed 0.015 astronomical units from Earth, about six times the distance to the Moon, the closest approach of any comet in recorded history. It has not been seen since 1770 and is lost.
events.html: The comet Charles Messier had discovered in June passed 0.015 astronomical units from Earth, about six times the distance to the Moon, the closest approach of any comet in recorded history. It has not been seen since 1770 and is lost.

events.title: Continental Congress debates independence in a decisive test vote
events.description: Meeting as a committee of the whole, Congress debated Richard Henry Lee's resolution for independence; nine colonies backed it in a test vote. The formal vote followed the next day with twelve in favour.
events.html: Meeting as a committee of the whole, Congress debated Richard Henry Lee's resolution for independence; nine colonies backed it in a test vote. The formal vote followed the next day with twelve in favour.

events.title: The Quinault and Quileute sign a treaty ceding land to the US
events.description: At the Quinault River in the recently formed Washington Territory, the Quinault and Quileute peoples of the western Olympic Peninsula signed a treaty ceding their land to the United States. Congress ratified it on 8 March 1859.
events.html: At the Quinault River in the recently formed Washington Territory, the Quinault and Quileute peoples of the western Olympic Peninsula signed a treaty ceding their land to the United States. Congress ratified it on 8 March 1859.

events.title: Union guns repel Lee's assaults at Malvern Hill
events.description: Massed Union artillery shattered Confederate attacks at Malvern Hill near Richmond, the last of the Seven Days Battles. Though McClellan withdrew afterwards, Lee's costly assaults ended the campaign.
events.html: Massed Union artillery shattered Confederate attacks at Malvern Hill near Richmond, the last of the Seven Days Battles. Though McClellan withdrew afterwards, Lee's costly assaults ended the campaign.

events.title: The Battle of Gettysburg begins in Pennsylvania
events.description: Confederate and Union forces collided at Gettysburg, opening the largest battle ever fought in North America. Three days later Lee's army withdrew, having suffered some 23,000 of the roughly 50,000 casualties.
events.html: Confederate and Union forces collided at Gettysburg, opening the largest battle ever fought in North America. Three days later Lee's army withdrew, having suffered some 23,000 of the roughly 50,000 casualties.

events.title: British army suffers 57,470 casualties on the first day of the Somme
events.description: After a week-long bombardment, British and French infantry attacked along the Somme. Britain lost 57,470 men killed, wounded or missing, the heaviest single-day toll in the British Army's history.
events.html: After a week-long bombardment, British and French infantry attacked along the Somme. Britain lost 57,470 men killed, wounded or missing, the heaviest single-day toll in the British Army's history.

events.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
events.description: At midnight sovereignty over Hong Kong passed from Britain to China, ending 156 years of British rule. The territory became a Special Administrative Region under the 'one country, two systems' principle.
events.html: At midnight sovereignty over Hong Kong passed from Britain to China, ending 156 years of British rule. The territory became a Special Administrative Region under the 'one country, two systems' principle.

song: Patriots of Buenos Aires in the wars of independence; later the Argentine Republic
A song written in Buenos Aires in 1813, during the fight for independence from Spain, that became Argentina's national anthem.
